title: MH370 Bathymetry
description:
The search for MH370 collected 278,000 square kilometres of bathymetry data within the search area and 710,000 square kilometres of data in total, which includes the data acquired in transit between port and the search area. It is one of the largest marine surveys ever conducted. The Phase One data provided maps that are at least 15 times higher resolution than the maps that were previously available. While the data was collected for the sole purpose of locating the missing aircraft, it will be of interest to the scientific community as it is some of the first high resolution data of this area of the sea floor. Data acquired during the search for MH370 is available for exploration and download from Geoscience Australia.


References

Kornei, K. (2017), Seafloor data from lost airliner search are publicly released, Eos, 98, https://doi.org/10.1029/2017EO078307.

licenseInfo:
Users can download the bathymetry data over the Indian Ocean which is licensed under Creative Commons.

Data can be downloaded from the portal at no charge and there is no limit to how many requests you can place (please check the file size before you download your results).

If you need datasets in full, please contact clientservices@ga.gov.au.
